The plot then gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture, waterlogging and season. At the existing threshold (12, or 60 for woody plants) the unit is absorbed into the new plant: it leaves the food stocks and its mass is recorded (cultivation-plot-established). Stock then grows by one unit per growth interval up to the ceiling (cultivation-crop-matured at the first unit) and is harvested only through unchanged gather. If the buried unit spoils first under the existing ageing law, the plot dies, stops growing and is no longer a food source (cultivation-trial-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge (cultivation-work-paused). Plant resumes the person's own unfinished work and pays only the remaining round (cultivation-work-resumed). End takes one round and no energy, acts only on the person's own unfinished work, returns the unit once in its current condition and clears the empty site (cultivation-trial-ended). Death before transfer leaves the unit where the person died. A transferred unit stays planted, and nothing is refunded. Inspect (one round, 0.2 energy) runs the baseline probe observation on a plot or plant source in reach and adds an unverified personal record of visible lifecycle, stage, stock, soil and weather (cultivation-condition-observed). Verified findings come only from the probe's existing dated-change rule, which deduplicates across probe and cultivation. Tend is refused before any cost. This scope has no carried water, fertilizer or soil amendment, no input can change a plot's moisture, and crowding affects only dispersal, so no treatment input or effect exists and treatment_applied is never emitted. Also not implemented: destructive sampling of a planted specimen (the probe's material modes need an owned unreserved stack and measure load, water or heat response, not viability, and digging up a buried unit is not represented; a unit can still be probed before planting), a stressed label, and any satisfaction. The planting event carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone, short pleasure or care satisfaction is awarded, and planting or failure gives no nutrition or comfort. Modeling assumptions: a whole harvested unit of a living plant is that plant's propagule, as in the dispersal law, for every food with a growth cycle and an ageing lifetime (so the root and berry, and also nuts, fruit, tubers and fungi). Hand preparation is limited to ordinary soil and needs no tool. The site conditions are the dispersal law's. Hand-loosened soil is not a lasting represented state, so ending or failing before transfer leaves no object. Water and nutrients are represented only by the growth rule's climate moisture, soil moisture, waterlogging and depletion terms, with no separate ledger. The plot keeps the source's growth interval and a stock ceiling of at most 4. A dead plot stays as an empty marked position. Plants that an established plot later disperses are ordinary plants. No energy, time or broken stems are refunded or restored. The completion event carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone is awarded, and no satisfaction, comfort or reward source is added; the experience review's optional short-pleasure and 0.2 sustained recognition were left out because the specification does not require them. Comfort: physical wellbeing (continuous-wellbeing.ts, v7Wellbeing) is recomputed every round as physicalCap x (0.3 x health/100 + 0.25 x satiety/100 + 0.25 x energy/energyCap + 0.2 x thermal comfort from body temperature) with no term for contact or cushioning, and the kernel rejects any action handler or environment response that writes wellbeing; the only inputs a package can reach are the vitals, and routing +0.5 through energy or body temperature would invent recovery or insulation that the specification excludes, so no honest path exists and the +0.5 contribution is omitted (trials record comfort 0); a cushioning term would need a separately reviewed change to the wellbeing rule. Unit mapping: one specification unit is one world unit of the fiber resource (dry grass: 0.1 mass per unit, obtained with the unchanged base gather at one round and 2 energy per unit from the finite source stock in interaction range); no source fact is exposed or pre-committed. Modeling assumptions: the world gives grass no stem length, diameter or count, so dimensions are declared and yield is mass-based: mass units are read as kilograms and a plaited thin-stem layer is taken to weigh 0.6 per m2, so two crossing layers over 0.45 x 0.45 m with x1.5 for overlapping ends and edges tucked back about 0.05 m per side need 0.3645 mass (3.7 dry-grass units, 1.5 reed units); the 4-unit recipe is therefore an allocation with a measured margin, and a shortfall arises only when part of the 4 units is broken fiber (tested scraps or worn recovered fiber); thin stem form is declared only for dry grass and reeds; the 0.4 flexibility threshold is twice ex16 branch-screen@1's open-weave value and below ex15 simple-shelter@1's 0.7 for wrapped binding because plaited crossings bend thin strips over about one strip width; there is no friction or tensile model, so tuck retention follows from flexibility and an intact sample; condition is the intact share of stems, and the largest opening 0.06 x (1 - condition) m ties the specification's 0.03 m limit to the ex15 sound condition 0.5; people have no body mass or posture, so a trial's load is one undifferentiated person, any living person whose position lies on the mat counts as occupying it, and slipping is excluded by the firm-ground precondition rather than computed; hands are not represented and are not checked; dry grass and reeds have decay rate 0, so holding fiber inside a mat changes no ageing; the mat is non-solid; only the maker may repair, lift, place or dismantle, and handing a mat to another person is not supported in this version. Grounded: real dry-grass units, escrow, mass, provenance and conservation in tenths, energy and round costs, ground conditions, probe-revealed material values, current rain and the existing carried-load rule. Not grounded (declared or approximated): stem geometry, the areal mass and allowance, the thin-stem list, the flexibility threshold, the opening relation, the absence of friction, posture and body mass, and the wear rates (taken from the specification).
